item.title: Hibiscus opens with a march
item.description: THE 70th FMF Hibiscus Festival will officially open with a march and parade from the Flea Market to Albert Park at 10am, signalling the start of this year’s celebrations. The opening program will feature an official ceremony, appearances by former queens and introductions of the festival contestants.
item.content:encoded:
THE 70th FMF Hibiscus Festival will officially open with a march and parade from the Flea Market to Albert Park at 10am, signalling the start of this year’s celebrations.

The opening program will feature an official ceremony, appearances by former queens and introductions of the festival contestants.

Entertainment will follow throughout the afternoon and evening, with performances from Laisa Vulakoro, Miles Manulevu, Manava Dance, Savuto, Taitusi Mareau and Via Ni Tebara, among others.

Meanwhile, as the FMF Hibiscus Festival marks its 70th anniversary, the charity chest continues to turn the event’s popularity into practical support for community organisations and people in need.

While the festival is known for its colourful celebrations and Queens contest, contributions through the charity chest provide assistance to groups that often operate with limited resources and little public support.

Festival director Ellen Whippy Knight said giving remained an important part of the festival’s identity, with every contribution helping extend its impact beyond the event itself.

“The charity chest reminds us that the Hibiscus Festival has always stood for something greater than entertainment and pageantry,” she said.

She said fundraising required hours of planning, promotion and personal appeals from those involved.

The initiative also provides an opportunity for businesses, individuals and festival supporters to contribute to causes supporting vulnerable and overlooked communities.

Queens contest coordinator Taniela Matanimeke said the campaign strengthened partnerships between contestants, businesses and the wider community.

“Behind the crown is a cause, and behind every contribution is an opportunity to make someone feel seen, supported and remembered,” he said.

With the festival reaching its 70th year, organisers say the charity chest remains a tangible way for the community to give back and ensure the celebration creates an impact beyond the stage.

item.title: Ballot paper to feature numbers
item.description: Fiji’s upcoming General Election will again feature numbers on the ballot paper, with the Electoral Commission preparing to conduct a ball draw to determine the first three digits to be used. Supervisor of Elections Ana Mataiciwa revealed the upcoming ball draw during a media briefing on the Fijian Elections Office’s preparations for the election.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji’s upcoming General Election will again feature numbers on the ballot paper, with the Electoral Commission preparing to conduct a ball draw to determine the first three digits to be used.

Supervisor of Elections Ana Mataiciwa revealed the upcoming ball draw during a media briefing on the Fijian Elections Office’s preparations for the election.

The FEO said one of its upcoming activities would be the “Electoral Commission’s ball draw for the first three digits on the ballot paper”.

The briefing also revealed that 1,508 provisional polling venues have been identified nationwide.

Of these, 880 are designated for Election Day and 628 for pre-poll voting, accommodating a total of 2,149 polling stations across the Central, Western, Northern and Eastern divisions.

Election official recruitment has also exceeded requirements.

The FEO has received 14,606 applications against a requirement for 8,907 election officials. So far, 13,449 officials have been recruited, with the current recruitment phase focusing on Suva, Nausori, Labasa and Lautoka.

Preparations for election training are also progressing, with 80 field trainers supporting the programme.

Training of Trainers sessions are scheduled for September, followed by election official training from September 15 to November 22.

The FEO said election materials, including ballot boxes, polling kits and voting screens, have been delivered and are ready for use.

Fiji currently has 11 registered political parties.

The FEO will also conduct its YES Outreach – Registration and Awareness Drive during October and November, focusing on voter registration and public awareness ahead of the General Election.

Following the briefing, FEO Manager Legal Mesake Dawai updated media representatives on proposed amendments to Fiji’s electoral laws.

item.title: Women escaping violence get safe haven
item.description: A new safe shelter for women escaping violence has been established in Lautoka, providing protection, counselling and support for those seeking to rebuild their lives. Minister for Women, Children and Social Protection Sashi Kiran said the Women’s Safe Shelter is being managed by Empower Pacific and is now fully equipped and staffed.
item.content:encoded:
A new safe shelter for women escaping violence has been established in Lautoka, providing protection, counselling and support for those seeking to rebuild their lives.

Minister for Women, Children and Social Protection Sashi Kiran said the Women’s Safe Shelter is being managed by Empower Pacific and is now fully equipped and staffed.

The facility was originally built by Soroptimist International on State-provided land and handed over to the Government in 2021, but remained closed.

Ms Kiran said when the Coalition Government took office, it identified the need for improvements to ensure the facility met safety, security and shelter compliance requirements.

She said LDS Charities subsequently invested $180,000 to upgrade the facility, while the Government provided an operational grant to enable the shelter to begin providing services.

“This shelter is a space where women escaping violence can find protection, counselling and support to begin rebuilding their lives,” Ms Kiran said.

She thanked Empower Pacific, Soroptimist International, LDS Charities and other partners involved in establishing and operating the facility.

Ms Kiran said cooperation across government, civil society and communities was essential to ensure women experiencing violence knew where they could seek assistance.

“We must work together to ensure that women experiencing violence know that support is available, that they are not alone, and that they have a pathway towards safety, healing and independence,” she said.

The Minister stressed that violence against women and girls should never become accepted as part of society.

“Violence against women and girls must never be accepted or normalised. Every woman deserves to live free from violence and fear,” Ms Kiran said.

item.title: Fiji issues safety advisory for nationals in Nepal and Tibet
item.description: The Fiji High Commission in New Delhi has issued a safety advisory for Fijian nationals currently in Nepal and Tibet, urging them to remain vigilant amid recent natural disasters and continuing risks in affected areas. The High Commission is advising Fijians to prioritise their personal safety and follow all instructions and advisories issued by local authorities.
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji High Commission in New Delhi has issued a safety advisory for Fijian nationals currently in Nepal and Tibet, urging them to remain vigilant amid recent natural disasters and continuing risks in affected areas.

The High Commission is advising Fijians to prioritise their personal safety and follow all instructions and advisories issued by local authorities.

Nationals have been urged to avoid affected, high-risk and restricted areas, particularly locations experiencing landslides, flooding, road closures and other hazards.

The advisory also calls on Fijians to avoid unnecessary travel to disaster-affected areas and to confirm the safety and accessibility of routes before undertaking any journey.

Fijians in Nepal and Tibet are also encouraged to maintain regular contact with family members and keep them informed of their location and wellbeing.

The High Commission says passports, identification, essential medicines, emergency supplies and communication devices should be kept readily accessible.

Nationals are further advised to monitor official weather, disaster-management and transport advisories, rather than relying solely on unverified information circulating on social media.

Where it is safe to do so, Fijians are encouraged to register or update their presence and contact details with the Fiji High Commission in New Delhi, particularly if they are in or travelling to affected areas.

The High Commission has also asked that any emergency, injury, missing person or difficulty making contact with a Fijian national be reported immediately.

The Fiji High Commission says it is closely monitoring the situation and will provide further updates as reliable information becomes available.

Fijian nationals requiring urgent consular assistance are encouraged to contact the High Commission in New Delhi at the earliest opportunity.

The High Commission has urged all Fijians in the affected areas to remain calm, vigilant and cautious, and to prioritise their safety at all times.

item.title: Fiji TV returns to breakeven after $15,000 profit
item.description: Fiji Television Limited has returned to breakeven after reversing losses from previous financial years, recording a profit before tax of $15,664 for the year ended June 30, 2026. The company says its audited FY2026 results mark an important turning point following restructuring, cost reductions and changes to its operations.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji Television Limited has returned to breakeven after reversing losses from previous financial years, recording a profit before tax of $15,664 for the year ended June 30, 2026.

The company says its audited FY2026 results mark an important turning point following restructuring, cost reductions and changes to its operations.

Fiji TV generated $3.85 million in revenue during the financial year, including $3.17 million from services rendered and $688,696 from communication and radio rental equipment sales.

It also recorded $551,175 in other income from sources including rental income, miscellaneous income and gains from the disposal of fixed assets.

Chief executive officer Sunjeewa Perera said the company’s first priority had been stopping its losses.

“When we began this journey, our first task was clear, we needed to stop the losses and bring the business back to breakeven. We have achieved that,” Mr Perera said.

“It required difficult decisions and a tremendous collective effort from our people.”

He said Fiji TV had reviewed how it operated, invested and deployed resources, with the focus now shifting towards increasing revenue.

“The next priority is to build revenues by responding to the way audiences and advertisers are changing,” he said.

Mr Perera said this would involve moving beyond the traditional television model, expanding Fiji TV’s digital presence, better utilising its content and capabilities and pursuing partnerships and new business opportunities.

Chairperson Nesbitt Hazelman said the board was encouraged by the turnaround.

“Moving from the losses of previous financial years to breakeven is an important step and demonstrates the impact of the changes undertaken across the Company,” Mr Hazelman said.

However, he stressed that the turnaround was only the beginning.

“The work is not complete. The emphasis now moves towards building the top line while continuing to operate responsibly.”

Fiji TV said FY2027 would focus on revenue growth, digital media, locally relevant content, partnerships and new services while maintaining careful control of expenditure.

“FY2026 has been about putting the business back on firm ground. FY2027 will be about building from it,” the company said.

item.title: Court orders FSC to reinstate sacked employee
item.description: The Employment Relations Court has ordered the Fiji Sugar Corporation to immediately reinstate a former weighbridge clerk after ruling that his dismissal almost four years ago was unlawful. Justice Dane Tuiqereqere, in a judgment delivered on August 21, allowed an appeal by Roniel Rohit Lal and quashed a 2024 Employment Relations Tribunal decision that had upheld his dismissal.
item.content:encoded:
The Employment Relations Court has ordered the Fiji Sugar Corporation to immediately reinstate a former weighbridge clerk after ruling that his dismissal almost four years ago was unlawful.

Justice Dane Tuiqereqere, in a judgment delivered on August 21, allowed an appeal by Roniel Rohit Lal and quashed a 2024 Employment Relations Tribunal decision that had upheld his dismissal.

Mr Lal had worked for FSC since June 2013 before his employment was terminated on August 8, 2022.

The dismissal followed allegations arising from an incident on July 26, 2022, including that Mr Lal had verbally and physically abused another employee, vandalised an FSC vehicle, was intoxicated and had verbally abused a general manager.

Justice Tuiqereqere found that while the Tribunal had determined that FSC had failed to prove the allegations, it had nevertheless concluded there was a valid reason to dismiss Mr Lal.

“The Tribunal’s findings cannot be reconciled with its conclusions,” Justice Tuiqereqere said.

He said if FSC’s allegations could not be proven, the correct conclusion was that the termination was unlawful, rather than merely procedurally unfair.

“As the allegations could not be proven, FSC could not demonstrate any gross misconduct,” the judge said.

“There was, therefore, no proper basis for FSC to terminate the appellant’s employment and no basis for the Tribunal to find that the termination was lawful.”

The court ordered Mr Lal to be reinstated immediately to his position as a weighbridge clerk.

However, Justice Tuiqereqere declined Mr Lal’s request for reimbursement of wages covering the period since his dismissal, finding that his behaviour during the incident was “less than satisfactory” and had contributed to the problems he subsequently faced.

The court instead awarded Mr Lal six months’ wages as compensation for humiliation, loss of dignity and injury to feelings arising from the unlawful termination.

FSC must pay the compensation, less the three months’ wages already paid under the Tribunal’s earlier order, within 30 days.

item.title: Court rules FICAC does not need DPP consent to prosecute duo
item.description: The High Court in Suva has ruled that the Fiji Independent Commission Against Corruption does not require the prior consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions to institute a charge of conspiracy to defraud. Justice Usaia Ratuvili delivered the ruling on August 25 in the case involving Pauliasi Tabualevu Bainivalu and Shiu Raman, who are facing several charges brought by FICAC.
item.content:encoded:
The High Court in Suva has ruled that the Fiji Independent Commission Against Corruption does not require the prior consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions to institute a charge of conspiracy to defraud.

Justice Usaia Ratuvili delivered the ruling on August 25 in the case involving Pauliasi Tabualevu Bainivalu and Shiu Raman, who are facing several charges brought by FICAC.

The first count alleges that Bainivalu and Raman conspired between January 2014 and July 2019 to dishonestly obtain a gain of $370,061.39 from the Nasinu Town Council. They have pleaded not guilty.

Raman’s counsel raised a preliminary objection, arguing that the conspiracy charge was procedurally invalid because FICAC had not obtained the DPP’s consent.

The defence relied on section 49(9) of the Crimes Act 2009, which states that proceedings for an offence of conspiracy require the consent of the DPP. It argued the absence of consent amounted to a fundamental defect and sought to have the first count struck out or dismissed.

FICAC opposed the application, arguing that its own legislation specifically gives it authority to prosecute conspiracy to defraud and allows the FICAC Commissioner to institute proceedings without DPP consent.

“The FICAC Act 2007, is very clear that FICAC has the authority to prosecute Conspiracy to Defraud in the name of the FICAC Commissioner,” Justice Ratuvili said.

“The Commissioner also does not need to obtain the consent of the DPP to file any charges listed in section 2A of the FICAC Act 2007.”

The court ruled that the conspiracy charge was properly before it and refused the application to dismiss or sever the count.

Justice Ratuvili concluded that “FICAC has the jurisdiction to institute charges for the offence of Conspiracy to Defraud in the name of the FICAC Commissioner and does not require the prior consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions to file these charges.”

The court said the matter would now take its own course.

item.title: Fiji business establishments rise to 20,563
item.description: The number of active business establishments operating across Fiji reached 20,563 in 2025, according to the Fiji Bureau of Statistics’ Experimental Statistical Business Register. The latest figures show the Suva, Nasinu, Lami and Navua corridor remains Fiji’s largest business hub, accounting for 7,630 establishments, or about 37 per cent of the total.
item.content:encoded:
The number of active business establishments operating across Fiji reached 20,563 in 2025, according to the Fiji Bureau of Statistics’ Experimental Statistical Business Register.

The latest figures show the Suva, Nasinu, Lami and Navua corridor remains Fiji’s largest business hub, accounting for 7,630 establishments, or about 37 per cent of the total.

Ba and Lautoka followed with 4,534 establishments, while Nadi and Sigatoka recorded 3,238.

Nakasi, Nausori and Korovou accounted for 2,266 establishments, Labasa, Savusavu and Seaqaqa had 2,148, while Rakiraki and Tavua recorded 747.

The statistics also show significant growth across several major industries.

Transport and Storage recorded the strongest increase, rising 40.5 per cent compared with 2024.

Accommodation and Food Service establishments increased by 15.7 per cent, Wholesale and Retail Trade by 11 per cent, Manufacturing by 9 per cent, while Education edged up by 0.2 per cent.

Wholesale and Retail Trade remained the largest of the five major industries, with 7,042 establishments in 2025, compared with 6,344 in 2024.

Transport and Storage increased from 2,002 establishments to 2,812, while Accommodation and Food Service rose from 1,311 to 1,517.

The register also shows sole traders remain the most common form of business ownership, accounting for 9,489 establishments.

There were 7,755 private limited companies, 1,739 non-profit organisations, 601 co-operatives, 561 partnerships, 199 trusts and estates, 116 statutory boards and 103 public limited companies.

The Bureau said the Statistical Business Register provides a comprehensive list of businesses and other entities engaged in producing goods and services in Fiji and is compiled using administrative data.

It cautioned that the 2025 figures are an experimental release, with the updating of establishments still continuing.
